files.name: Name
files.truncated: Only the first {{count}} entries are shown.
files.skipped_one: {{count}} entry with a name Pulsar cannot open is not shown.
files.skipped_other: {{count}} entries with names Pulsar cannot open are not shown.
files.hiddenInName: This name has hidden characters. It reads: {{name}}
files.deleteFolderConfirm: Delete the folder {{name}} and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
files.busy: An operation is changing this server's files: changes are blocked until it ends.
files.nodeOffline: The node is offline: files cannot be changed until it reconnects.

nameProblems.characters: Names cannot contain \ / : * ? " < > | or control characters.
nameProblems.dots: Names cannot be . or .., start with a space or end with a dot or a space.
nameProblems.reserved: Windows reserves that name (CON, NUL, COM1…).

uploads.label: Uploading {{name}}
uploads.exists: A file with that name already exists.

editor.label: Contents of {{name}}
editor.conflict: The file changed on the server since you opened it. Reload it (your changes are lost) or overwrite it with yours.
editor.tooLarge: This file is larger than 1 MB: download it instead.
editor.binary: This file is not UTF-8 text, so it cannot be edited here: download it instead.
editor.mixedEndings: This file mixes Windows and Unix line endings, and saving it here would change them: it is shown read only. Download it to edit it.
editor.tabHint: Tab indents. To leave the editor with the keyboard, press Esc and then Tab, or Ctrl+M (Shift+Alt+M on a Mac) to make Tab move the focus.

addons.hint: Mods and mod frameworks this game's template knows. The node downloads their latest release from their authors' GitHub and installs it only when it matches the checksum GitHub publishes. They are made by third parties, under their own licences.
addons.stopToChange: Stop the server to install, update or remove mods.
addons.reinstallAfterUpdate: Game updates overwrite it: it is installed again after each update.

refused.conflicts: {{name}} cannot be installed with {{others}}: remove it first.

addons.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}} from {{server}}? The files it installed are deleted, even if you changed them; files you added yourself are kept.

backups.title: Backups
backups.hint: Backups are zip files kept on the server's node. They hold the files the game's template chooses (its configuration, its add-ons), not what can be downloaded again.
backups.name: Name
backups.nameHint: Optional. Without one, the backup is named after the time it was made.
backups.runningWarning: The server is running: the game is asked to save first (when its template says how) and its files are copied from a snapshot of the disk. If the node cannot take one, files the game writes meanwhile may be copied half written; the backup will say so.
backups.restoreText: The backup's files replace the current ones in {{server}}.
backups.restoreKeep: Files the backup does not have stay as they are.
backups.restoreClean: Delete the files made after this backup
backups.restoreCleanHint: Files the backup would include but does not have are deleted first, such as map regions explored since. The installed game and files outside the backup stay.
backups.restoreCleanSkipped: Not available: this backup left out files the game held open, and restoring clean would delete them.

copy.snapshot: Copied from a snapshot of the disk
copy.live: Copied while the game ran, without a snapshot ({{reason}})

save.waited: the game was asked to save first
save.unconfirmed: the game did not confirm its save

snapshotErrors.disabled: snapshots are turned off on this node
snapshotErrors.not_permitted: the agent is not running as an administrator
snapshotErrors.unavailable: the Volume Shadow Copy service is not running
snapshotErrors.no_space: the disk has no room for the snapshot
snapshotErrors.failed: Windows could not take one; the agent's log says why
snapshotErrors.game_started: the game started while its files were read

backups.stopToRestore: Stop the server to restore a backup.
backups.deleteConfirm: Delete the backup {{name}}? Its file is removed from the node. This cannot be undone.

retention.title: Retention
retention.hint: After each new backup, the oldest ones beyond this number are deleted. Locked backups are always kept and do not count.
retention.invalid: A whole number from 1 to {{max}}, or empty to keep them all.
retention.notANumber: Type a whole number, or leave it empty to keep them all.
retention.confirm_one: Keep only the newest backup? Older unlocked ones are deleted now.
retention.confirm_other: Keep only the {{count}} newest backups? Older unlocked ones are deleted now.

remote.title: Remote copy
remote.hint: Each new backup is also copied to remote storage, so it survives the loss of this node. A backup the node no longer has is brought back from there to restore or download it.
remote.none: The panel has no backup storage yet: settings managers add one in Administration → Backup storage.

schedules.title: Scheduled tasks
schedules.hint: Tasks run at their time in the time zone you choose, following its daylight saving time. The panel runs them: while it is not running, nothing runs, and missed runs are recorded rather than done late.
schedules.name: Name
schedules.commandHint: Sent as if typed in the console; skipped while the server is not running.
schedules.updateHint: An update needs the server stopped: schedule a stop before it and a start after it.
schedules.onlyIfRunning: Only while the server is running
schedules.cronHint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. For example, 30 5 * * 1-5 is 05:30 on weekdays.
schedules.timeZoneHint: The task runs at that time there, following its daylight saving time.
schedules.timeZoneUnknown: Your browser does not know the time zone {{zone}}: the next runs are shown in UTC.
schedules.deleteConfirm: Delete the task {{name}} and its history?
schedules.missed_one: Missed: the panel was not running.
schedules.missed_other: {{count}} runs missed: the panel was not running.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.hint: For scripts and tools: send a key as "Authorization: Bearer <key>". It acts as you, with your permissions or only the ones you choose, and never reaches your account, password or keys.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.revokeConfirm: Revoke {{name}}? Whatever uses it stops working now.
apiKeys.createdIntro: Copy it now: it is shown only this once. Keep it like a password.
apiKeys.usage: Send it in every request as: Authorization: Bearer <key>

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.intro: Besides your password, sign-in asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password…).
twoFactor.scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
twoFactor.qrLabel: QR code for your authenticator app
twoFactor.manual: If you cannot scan it, enter this key in the app:
twoFactor.codesIntro: Save these recovery codes somewhere safe, away from your phone. Each one signs you in once if you lose the app. They are shown only now.
twoFactor.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying. Select the text and copy it by hand.
twoFactor.requiredByRole: One of your roles requires it.
twoFactor.newCodesDescription: The codes you have now stop working.
twoFactor.turnOffDescription: Sign-in will ask only for your password.
twoFactor.requiredSubtitle: One of your roles requires it. Set it up to continue.
twoFactor.loginApp: Enter the code your authenticator app shows.
twoFactor.loginRecovery: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each one works once.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Get told on Discord or by email when a server crashes, a backup fails or a node goes offline.
notifications.noChannels: No channels yet. Add one to start getting notified.
notifications.name: Name
notifications.serversHint: Server events only for the chosen servers. Node events go to every channel that wants them.
notifications.webhookHint: In Discord: channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook → Copy webhook URL.
notifications.webhookKeep: Leave it empty to keep the current webhook ({{id}}).
notifications.recipientsHint: Up to 10, one per line or separated by commas.
notifications.emailNeedsSmtp: Email channels need the SMTP server in the settings below.
notifications.deleteConfirm: Delete the channel {{name}}? Its message history goes too.
notifications.panelUrlHint: How people reach the panel, for links in messages (e.g. https://panel.example.com:8443). Empty: no links.
notifications.emailOff: Email is off until an SMTP server is set.

securities.none: None (a relay on this network without signing in, or on this machine)

notifications.smtpPasswordKeep: Leave it empty to keep the saved password (only while the server and user stay the same).

storage.title: Backup storage
storage.description: S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO…) that servers copy their backups to.
storage.empty: No storage yet. Add one, then choose it in a server's Backups tab.
storage.name: Name
storage.endpointHint: The service's address. Empty for AWS S3. Backblaze B2: https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com. Plain http only on your local network.
storage.regionHint: auto for Cloudflare R2; the bucket's region for AWS and B2; us-east-1 for most others.
storage.secretKeep: Leave it empty to keep the saved key.
storage.pathStyle: Bucket in the path (most S3-compatible services need it; AWS does not)
storage.keysHint: Give these keys access to this bucket only. Nodes get them inside each backup command and keep nothing.
storage.deleteConfirm: Delete the storage {{name}}? Backups already copied stay in the bucket.

history.title: Usage history
history.empty: No usage recorded in this period yet. It is recorded while the server runs.
history.emptyNode: No usage recorded in this period yet. It is recorded while the node is connected.
history.chartLabel: {{chart}} over time; use the arrow keys to read each point

databases.title: Databases
databases.hint: MySQL/MariaDB databases for the game and its plugins. Each one has a user of its own that can only use it; put the address, name, user and password in the plugin's configuration.
databases.noHosts: No database host is available for this server's node: an administrator adds them under Database hosts.
databases.full: The server has as many databases as it may have.
databases.name: Name
databases.nameHint: The database (and its user) will be {{name}}.
databases.nameInvalid: 1 to 20 lowercase letters, digits and underscores.
databases.rotateConfirm: Give {{name}} a new password? The game stops connecting until its configuration has the new one.
databases.deleteConfirm: Delete {{name}} and everything in it? This cannot be undone.

databaseHosts.title: Database hosts
databaseHosts.description: MySQL or MariaDB servers where servers get their databases. The panel connects to them with an account that may create databases and users.
databaseHosts.name: Name
databaseHosts.addressHint: Where the panel reaches the database server: a host name or an IP address.
databaseHosts.userNameHint: An account that may create databases and users (and grant them).
databaseHosts.passwordKeep: Leave it empty to keep the current one.
databaseHosts.serverAddressHint: When game servers reach it at another address (127.0.0.1 if it runs on their node). Empty: the same.
databaseHosts.userHostHint: Where the database users may connect from: % for anywhere, or an address or pattern such as 10.0.0.%.
databaseHosts.nodesHint: Servers of these nodes may use it. None ticked: every node.
databaseHosts.nodesKept_one: The host stays limited to the node it has.
databaseHosts.nodesKept_other: The host stays limited to the {{count}} nodes it has.
databaseHosts.nodesAll: With no node ticked, servers of every node may use this host.
databaseHosts.requireTlsHint: The panel connects only with TLS (it does not check the certificate). Off, it uses TLS when the server offers it and plain text otherwise, its account's password included. On by default unless the address is this machine or your local network.

steamAccounts.title: Steam accounts
steamAccounts.description: Accounts SteamCMD signs in with, for dedicated servers only an account that owns the game may download.
steamAccounts.empty: No Steam accounts yet: SteamCMD signs in anonymously.
steamAccounts.name: Name
steamAccounts.passwordKeep: Leave it empty to keep the current one.
steamAccounts.secondary: Use an account of its own for servers, not your personal one: Steam may ask for a Steam Guard code, and the agents keep the login SteamCMD caches (encrypted, never in a server's files).
steamAccounts.hint: The first install or update with an account may stop for a Steam Guard code (by mail, or from the Steam mobile app): the server's page asks for it. After that the node signs in with the login it keeps.

enrollmentTokens.title: Reusable enrollment tokens
enrollmentTokens.description: One token enrolls many machines, each as a new node named after it: for the agent MSI deployed with Intune or a group policy, or a script.
enrollmentTokens.empty: There are no reusable tokens. Nodes are added one at a time with their own command.
enrollmentTokens.noneUsable: No token can enroll machines now.
enrollmentTokens.name: Name
enrollmentTokens.nameHint: What it is for, e.g. "Intune rollout".
enrollmentTokens.maxUsesHint: How many machines can enroll with it (1 to 1000).
enrollmentTokens.requireApproval: New nodes wait for my approval
enrollmentTokens.requireApprovalHint: Recommended: if the token leaks, a machine that is not yours gets nothing until someone approves it.
enrollmentTokens.noApprovalWarning: Anyone with the token can add a node, until it expires, is used up or you revoke it.
enrollmentTokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke {{name}}? No machine can enroll with it anymore; the nodes it created stay.
enrollmentTokens.once: The token is shown only now. Use it with the agent MSI (silent install) or the installer script, on each machine as administrator:
enrollmentTokens.limits: It enrolls up to {{uses}} machines until {{expires}}, and you can revoke it at any time.
enrollmentTokens.approvalNote: The nodes it creates wait for your approval in this page before their agents connect.
enrollmentTokens.noApprovalNote: The nodes it creates are active right away.
enrollmentTokens.msiNote: {{file}} is in the release, next to the ZIP. The token reaches the machine on the command line: deploy it only through channels you trust.

agentTransport.title: Agent connections
agentTransport.description: On the panel's agents' address, every agent presents its node key as a TLS client certificate: a stolen session token is worth nothing without the node's key. Agents that can move there do so on their own and keep the main address as a fallback.
agentTransport.noEndpoint: This panel has no agents' address. Add the Kestrel endpoint "Agents" (the installer's -AgentsPort) to use client certificates.
agentTransport.notInEffect: Certificates are required, but without an agents' address the requirement is not in effect.
agentTransport.allWithCertificate: Every enrolled node connects with its client certificate.
agentTransport.withoutCertificate_one: {{count}} node still connects without a client certificate:
agentTransport.withoutCertificate_other: {{count}} nodes still connect without a client certificate:
agentTransport.requireHint: Required: agents that reach the main address are sent to the agents' address, and sessions without a certificate end. Agents too old to move cannot connect until they are updated.
agentTransport.requireConfirm_one: {{count}} node still connects without a certificate. Its session ends now; an agent that can move goes to the agents' address, an older one cannot connect until it is updated. Require certificates?
agentTransport.requireConfirm_other: {{count}} nodes still connect without a certificate. Their sessions end now; agents that can move go to the agents' address, older ones cannot connect until they are updated. Require certificates?
agentTransport.stopRequiringConfirm: Let agents connect to the main address with the session token alone again?
